[ESTIMATE] While the plant's location in Hungary's industrial northeast suggests reasonable grid infrastructure quality, the capacity gap of ~197 MWe indicates the transmission system would require significant upgrading to handle SMR output. [INFERENCE] The 60+ year operational history proves grid connectivity exists, providing a foundation for upgrades, but the original infrastructure is likely inadequate for the higher SMR capacity without substantial reinforcement.

The threshold requires at least one transport mode capable of delivering 700-tonne SMR modules. [FACT] The Tiszapalkonya power station is located in Northern Hungary near the Tisza River, approximately 15 km southwest of Nyíregyháza. [FACT] Hungarian coal plants of this vintage (1952) and capacity (265 MWe) were typically served by rail infrastructure for coal delivery, as road transport was inadequate for the millions of tonnes of coal required over the plant's 60-year operational life. [INFERENCE] The plant's location in the Tisza valley, a major transport corridor, strongly suggests rail connectivity to the Hungarian national rail network (MÁV). [ESTIMATE] The nearest mainline railway is approximately 2-5 km from the site coordinates, well within the acceptable threshold for heavy module transport. The estimated transport access capability significantly exceeds the threshold requirement, therefore the site passes this criterion.
